html:
In April 1204 the army of the Fourth Crusade and the fleet of Venice stormed Constantinople and sacked it for three days. The capital of the Byzantine Empire, never before taken by a foreign army, was stripped of centuries of treasure.

The crusaders had come to put a pretender on the throne in the siege of 1203. When he failed to pay them and was murdered, they attacked, and broke in on 12 April. Churches, palaces and libraries were plundered and many citizens were killed. Relics and works of art were carried west; the four bronze horses of St Mark's Basilica in Venice came from the Hippodrome.

The conquerors then divided the empire. Baldwin of Flanders was crowned in Hagia Sophia as the first emperor of the Latin Empire, and Venice took ports and islands. Greek states rose in exile, among them the Empire of Nicaea, which retook the city in 1261. The empire never recovered its strength, and the sack sealed the split between the churches.
sum: In April 1204 the army of the Fourth Crusade and the fleet of Venice stormed Constantinople and sacked it for three days. The capital of the Byzantine Empire, never before taken by a foreign army, was stripped of centuries of treasure.
